topic: VLA或者WAM结合agent/vlm做子任务规划或者记忆任务
purpose: Independent known-item recall and screening regression set; never inject these titles or IDs into generated retrieval queries.
limitations: This is a small purposive sample, not an exhaustive bibliography or a statistically representative precision estimate.
Positive labels concern topic relevance, not scientific quality or reproducibility of the paper's claims.
Compute known-item recall only over positive papers whose original publication year satisfies the requested year_from. Conference year and revision year are not first-publication year.
Count retrieval recall before screening and retained recall after screening separately. Report missing titles explicitly.
Negative cases measure specific failure modes, not precision over the whole search result set.
Verify metadata against the linked primary source when refreshing this fixture; titles and withdrawal status can change.

semantics.screening: A paper can match planning without memory, or memory without task decomposition. Strong contributions to a constituent subtopic are relevant even if the abstract does not literally contain every abbreviation.

papers.title: Scaling World Model for Hierarchical Manipulation Policies
papers.reason: A high-level world model creates visual subgoals and a low-level VLA executes them; this directly covers world-model-assisted task decomposition.

papers.title: HiVLA: A Visual-Grounded-Centric Hierarchical Embodied Manipulation System
papers.reason: A VLM planner generates subtask instructions and target bounding boxes for a separate action expert. This directly tests the planning branch without requiring a memory contribution.

papers.title: World Action Planner: Generalizable Robot Decision-Making with Action-Conditioned World Models
aliases: World Action Planner: Generalizable Decision-Making with Action-Conditioned World Models
papers.reason: Combines VLM reasoning with an action-conditioned world model; the agent searches and refines action plans through imagined rollouts.

papers.title: HiMe: Hierarchical Embodied Memory for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Control
papers.reason: Separates a fast action executor, working-memory sentry, and long-term planner; cross-modal memory supports long-horizon control.

papers.title: Plan First, Act Later: Streaming Reasoning for Executable Memory in Robot Control
papers.reason: Uses a hierarchical memory framework in which a VLM selects a relevant subtask and a low-level VLA executes it. Also tests recall of very recent work.

papers.title: ReMem-VLA: Empowering Vision-Language-Action Model with Memory via Dual-Level Recurrent Queries
papers.reason: Adds explicit recurrent memory to VLA control for history-dependent manipulation. Relevant to the memory branch even without a separate high-level agent.

papers.title: HELM: Harness-Enhanced Long-horizon Memory for Vision-Language-Action Manipulation
papers.reason: Combines episodic memory, a state verifier, and a controller for rollback/replanning around VLA execution, directly addressing long-horizon task memory.

papers.title: Hi Robot: Open-Ended Instruction Following with Hierarchical Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.reason: A high-level VLM reasons over instructions and feedback to select the next step, then a low-level policy performs it. A 2026-only first-publication filter correctly excludes this important 2025 paper.

papers.title: MemoryVLA: Perceptual-Cognitive Memory in Vision-Language-Action Models for Robotic Manipulation
papers.reason: A pretrained VLM produces working-memory tokens, retrieves from a perceptual-cognitive memory bank, and conditions a diffusion action expert. First appeared in 2025, despite a 2026 revision/conference.

papers.title: HAMSTER: Hierarchical Action Models For Open-World Robot Manipulation
papers.reason: A high-level VLM predicts a coarse visual path that guides a low-level manipulation policy. This is relevant hierarchical planning even though it does not require literal 'task decomposition' wording.

papers.title: OpenVLA: An Open-Source Vision-Language-Action Model
papers.reason: Useful backbone background, but its main contribution is an open generalist VLA and efficient adaptation, not task memory or high-level subtask planning. Tests against retaining every VLA paper as a direct match.

papers.title: mzCache: On-Device LLM Memory Management under Multitasking
papers.reason: Operating-system/inference memory management is unrelated to a robot remembering task events, despite sharing 'memory' and 'multitasking'.

papers.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
papers.reason: KV-cache memory allocation for LLM serving does not address embodied planning or episodic/task memory.

papers.title: Explicit Language Memory for Long-Horizon Planning in Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.reason: Topically relevant but the primary arXiv page marks v3 withdrawn. Must be flagged and excluded from the endorsed evidence set, not treated as a topical false positive.

workflow_reference.name: PaperQA
applicable_ideas: Separate candidate discovery, relevance/evidence assessment, and synthesis.
Iterate between broad and narrow queries rather than requiring all topic facets in every query.
Keep provenance and score evidence relative to the question.
Do not equate a local-PDF answer pipeline with exhaustive global scholarly search.
